result:
Not quite ready to write it up yet. Two things are still open, and the design would rest on both.

First, what we picked covers one step: cleaning up each recording. The bigger choice is how the whole guide gets built. That means where it lives, how a volunteer uploads from their phone without anyone technical, and how a scan finds the right story in the right language. Your site is static pages on Netlify. That rules out some options and makes others cheap, so the choice deserves its own short comparison. I'll lay that out next with my recommendation.

Second, I don't yet know why the museum wants this. Before I compare ways to build it, I'd like to understand that. A guide meant to help visitors who can't read small labels would be built differently from one meant to add depth for enthusiasts or to reach Welsh speakers better.

So: what's prompting the audio guide now, and what would make you say it was worth it a year from now?
